title: Build it: the monsoon chart
summary: A brief and hidden tests: the city’s newsletter wants a chart of the year’s rain for its monsoon issue. Read weather.csv, draw the bars, write a headline from the data, label it, save monsoon.png and print a short summary. It must work for any city’s file.
objectives: Plan a chart program from a brief.
Combine reading, drawing, labelling and saving in one program.
Print a summary that matches the chart.

slides.say: “One chart: the year’s rain, with a headline readers remember. And the total for the caption.” Your program must work for whichever city’s weather.csv it is given.
points: Bars of **Rain_mm** by **Month**, one colour, on a figure **8 × 4**.
Title: **Jul is the wettest month: 310 mm** (worked out from the data).
Print the total, the wettest month and **Saved monsoon.png**.

Build it. From **weather.csv**: bars of **Rain_mm** by **Month** in **"tab:blue"** on a figure **8 wide, 4 high**; the title worked out from the data, like **Jul is the wettest month: 310 mm**; x label **Month**; y label **Rain (mm)**; save **monsoon.png**. Then print:

tasks.model:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
df = pd.read_csv("weather.csv")
wet = df.loc[df["Rain_mm"].idxmax()]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.bar(df["Month"], df["Rain_mm"], color="tab:blue")
ax.set_title(f"{wet['Month']} is the wettest month: {wet['Rain_mm']} mm")
ax.set_xlabel("Month")
ax.set_ylabel("Rain (mm)")
fig.savefig("monsoon.png")
print(f"Total rain: {df['Rain_mm'].sum()} mm")
print(f"Wettest: {wet['Month']} ({wet['Rain_mm']} mm)")
print("Saved monsoon.png")
